clue.text: Scottish symbols left out in ironic pieces

parts.note: the saltire is the diagonal St Andrew's cross on Scotland's flag

explanation.surface: A heraldry note about flags missing from some mocking artwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left out' reads as one phrase meaning omitted; split it, and 'left' is the L while 'out' says remove it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: satires are writings that mock through irony, so 'ironic pieces' describes them.

clue.text: First to snatch key amid the rioting shows sneakiness

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so the key goes into the middle of the other letters
a rioting crowd is disorderly, so the letters of THE break out of order
the first letter of the next word, 'snatch', is all that is taken

parts.note: THE mixed to TEH, split around the key
the Alt key on a computer keyboard
the last letter of the mixed TEH

explanation.surface: A looter grabbing something first in the chaos of a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' is a computer key here, ALT, not a musical key or a door key.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: stealth is the quality of acting secretly, which is sneakiness.

clue.text: Leaves magistrates imprisoning Rector for drinking sessions

parts.note: tea leaves, tea being made of them

indicators.note: a prison holds someone inside it

parts.note: beak is British slang for a magistrate

explanation.surface: Magistrates jailing a clergyman before going off for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb (departs) but is tea leaves; 'beak' is old British slang for a magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful description: a tea break is a short pause spent drinking tea, so a drinking session of a mild sort.

clue.text: Perhaps Vaughan Williams recording receiving cheer? On the contrary

indicators.note: to receive is to take in, so one piece goes inside the other
the opposite of what was said: the cheer receives the recording, not the recording the cheer

explanation.surface: A question about a recording of the composer Vaughan Williams being cheered.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the recording would take in the cheer; 'On the contrary' flips that, so RAH holds LP.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the composer Ralph Vaughan Williams is one Ralph, and 'Perhaps' flags that.

clue.text: Acrobatic toy was high — about time? That is about time

parts.note: meat that is high smells, so was high = stunk

explanation.surface: A toy that flew high, and a remark that it took long enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was high' means smelled bad, as game or meat does, not flew high. Both 'about time' pieces wrap a T.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: a stunt kite is steered through loops and dives, so it is a toy that does acrobatics.

clue.text: Conservative, challenged, losing head, snickered

indicators.note: a word's head is its first letter

parts.note: tackled = challenged; minus its first letter gives ACKLED

explanation.surface: A Tory, challenged and humiliated, laughing it off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing head' sounds like losing one's temper, but it only beheads the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: to cackle and to snicker are both to laugh in a harsh or sly way.

clue.text: Lead meeting to ditch hot, old African city

indicators.note: to ditch something is to get rid of it

parts.note: to chair = to lead a meeting; minus H gives CAIR

explanation.surface: Someone chairing a meeting about an old African city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead meeting' reads as a noun, the main meeting, but it is the verb 'chair'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Cairo, the Egyptian capital, is one of Africa's cities.

clue.text: Queen relocated to palace, embracing King

indicators.note: things relocated are moved to new places, so the letters of TO PALACE move around
to embrace is to hold within the arms

explanation.surface: A queen moving into a palace, arm in arm with a king.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits Cleopatra herself, who did embrace kings; the queen is the answer and the anagram both.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Cleopatra was a queen of Egypt, so she is one instance of a queen.

clue.text: Ranch equipment to remain fresh, trimmed in this way

indicators.note: trimming cuts off the end

parts.note: food that lasts stays fresh; minus T gives LAS
so = in this way, as in 'do it so'

explanation.surface: Advice on keeping ranch gear in good order by trimming it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remain fresh' is a food phrase; the verb that fits is 'last'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a lasso is the looped rope cowboys use on a ranch to catch cattle.

clue.text: Unhappy party line about distribution of fuel

indicators.note: distributing deals things out afresh, so the letters of FUEL are dealt out in a new order

explanation.surface: A gloomy political party line on how fuel is shared out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party line' reads as a policy, but splits into a do and an L.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: doleful describes a mournful, unhappy look or mood.

clue.text: I will block rejection of unconvincing message

indicators.note: a block stands in the middle of a path, so I goes into the middle of the other word
a rejected thing is sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a lame excuse is unconvincing; reversed to EMAL

explanation.surface: Someone vowing to stop a weak message from being turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I will' reads as a promise, but 'I' is the letter and 'will block' the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: an email is one kind of message.

clue.text: Film company runs a live broadcast

indicators.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it widely, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A film studio running a live television broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' fits the film-and-TV surface so well that it hides its job of mixing letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Universal Pictures is one of the big Hollywood studios.

clue.text: Musical piece: singer tailing off in front of non-mainstream group

parts.note: a lark is a songbird; minus K gives LAR
a ghetto is a community set apart from the mainstream

explanation.surface: A fading singer fronting an alternative band.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'singer' is a bird, not a vocalist; the band picture is all surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a larghetto is a movement marked to be played fairly slowly, so a musical piece.

clue.text: Possible result of investigation: academic with double character

indicators.note: to double something is to make two of it

parts.note: a character is a letter; here the O of PROF, added a second time

explanation.surface: A detective's findings about a two-faced professor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double character' sounds like a two-faced person; it means one letter of PROF appears twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: an investigation may or may not end in proof, which the word 'Possible' allows for.

clue.text: Keep a big audience, say, on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard, not seen, so the word is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: a horde is a big crowd

explanation.surface: A radio station trying to keep its large audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks the horde as one example of a big audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: to hoard is to keep things stored up rather than use them.

clue.text: Air support picked up one's identification

indicators.note: picking something up lifts it, and in a down entry lifting means reading upwards

explanation.surface: Air support picking up a plane's identifying marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air support' reads as military aircraft; it is a tune plus help.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a diagnosis is the identification of an illness.

clue.text: Impression received by two clubs almost entirely the same

indicators.note: almost means not quite all

parts.note: all = entirely; minus the last L gives AL

explanation.surface: A mark left by two golf clubs that are almost exactly alike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two clubs' reads as a pair; it is II then C, and 'almost entirely' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: identical means exactly the same.

clue.text: A source of wealth? It's sick, without question, getting surprised comment about individual

parts.note: queasy = sick; minus QU gives EASY

explanation.surface: Someone feeling ill and exclaiming over a person's fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: QU is a standard abbreviation for question; 'without question' sounds like 'certainly' but removes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose description: easy money is cash gained with little effort, one route to wealth, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Person in legal affair getting tense, in a stew

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another

parts.note: a soul = a person, as in 'not a soul'

explanation.surface: Someone caught up in a lawsuit, getting anxious and flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a stew' is an idiom for flustered, but the stew is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: cassoulet is a French dish of beans and meat, one kind of stew.

clue.text: Spanish percussion and Scottish rock in Lloyd Webber musical

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another

parts.note: Cats, the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical

explanation.surface: A West End show mixing Spanish percussion with Scottish rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' suggests music in this theatrical surface; it is a stone, in Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: castanets are the hand-held clappers of Spanish dance, a percussion instrument.

clue.text: Painstaking official probing birth membrane

indicators.note: a probe is pushed into something

parts.note: a caul is membrane sometimes covering a newborn's head

explanation.surface: A meticulous medical officer examining tissue from a birth.
explanation.walkthrough: The medical surface makes 'official' sound like a doctor; it is a sports referee.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: careful and painstaking both mean taking great pains over detail.

clue.text: Energy in assistant is something useful

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another

explanation.surface: Praise for an energetic assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a fair compliment: an energetic assistant really is an asset.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: an asset is anything of value or use.

clue.text: Youngster supporting viewpoint is distraught

indicators.note: a support holds something up from below

explanation.surface: A child backing a point of view that turns out to be upsetting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes on' here is the old sense of making a fuss, as in 'don't take on so'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to take on is to get worked up and upset, so someone who takes on is distraught.

clue.text: Continue to split Yorkshire city

explanation.surface: A plan to keep dividing a Yorkshire city.
explanation.walkthrough: Ripon is a small cathedral city in North Yorkshire; the order is read as 'continue' tacked on to 'to split', not the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Ripon holds city status and lies in Yorkshire.

clue.text: Expressionless when absorbing racy picture

explanation.surface: Someone keeping a straight face while looking at a risque picture.
explanation.walkthrough: Po-faced is British for humourlessly solemn, so PO stands for expressionless.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: photo is the everyday short form of photograph, a picture.

clue.text: Mike capturing dismissive sound after company's funny scenes here

indicators.note: a captor holds a prisoner

parts.note: CO = company, with 's joining it to the rest
to take the mike or the mick is to tease

explanation.surface: A microphone picking up a firm's jeering at comedy sketches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mike' and 'mick' are interchangeable in the British phrase 'take the mickey', to mock someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: a comic book is where funny scenes are drawn, so 'here' points to it.

clue.text: Engrave Harold's initial in piece of luggage

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another

explanation.surface: Having your initial engraved on your suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: Chase is a metalworking term here, not the everyday 'pursue'.
explanation.definitionFit: A craft sense: in metalwork, chasing is decorating a surface by engraving or embossing it.

clue.text: Pessimist in Surrey finally turned up, blocking County Council

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the last letter of Surrey is used
a block stands in the middle of a path, so the letters sit between the two Cs
turning something up flips it upward, and in a down entry that reads IN backwards

explanation.surface: A doom-monger turning up at a Surrey council meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is the link; the second is the word turned over. Surrey is a county south of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a cynic expects the worst of people's motives, much as a pessimist expects the worst.

clue.text: Fellow sadly wrong about spring as source of amphibians

indicators.note: things that go sadly go badly, so the letters of WRONG come out in poor order

parts.note: anagram of WRONG, split around SPA
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: A man mistaken about a spring being where frogs come from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' tempts as the season when frogs spawn, but it is a spa.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: frogspawn is the mass of eggs from which frogs, which are amphibians, hatch.

clue.text: Invalidates lines in newspaper after backlash?

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another
a lash back sends something the other way

parts.note: the Sun, a British newspaper; reversed to NUS

explanation.surface: A newspaper retracting lines after a public backlash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backlash' reads as public anger; broken into back-lash it sends the paper backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to null a thing is to make it void, which is to invalidate it.

clue.text: Quick scan: beauty, grace and allure at last

indicators.note: at last means at the end, so only the final letters of grace and allure are used

explanation.surface: A quick once-over at someone's beauty, grace and charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' applies to both grace and allure, giving two Es.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal synonym: a look-see is a brief inspection, a quick scan.

clue.text: Recalled vote against including University guy in part of Mexican trip

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the vote reads backwards
to include is to hold within

parts.note: nay = a no vote; reversed to YAN
cat = a guy, in jazz slang

explanation.surface: A recalled vote about a university man on holiday in Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' is a cat in hipster slang, not a rope or an effigy.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: the Yucatan peninsula is a region of Mexico that a trip there might take in.
